reasoning: The two attempts are nearly the same: server-side ownership table, shared rate limit, reach check against the recorded cell, a client-side pre-filter using the attribute, and TouchLongPress handling. A passes every check, and its right-click drag detection adds up mouse Delta, which works while the camera locks the cursor. B's position comparison barely catches a drag, so it leans on its 0.3 s timer. B fails StyLua in its own code. B's Destroying cleanup is a real plus, but it doesn't outweigh the formatting failure and the weaker right-click detection.

criteria.note: Removal is added to BlockPlacement.server.luau and BlockPlacer.luau in their existing style, with a RemoveBlock remote that mirrors PlaceBlock; no new framework or layout.
The server's own placedBlocks[part] = {Cell, OwnerUserId} table decides ownership, and the comment says the replicated attribute is never trusted.

Checks typeof Instance; looking the block up in the server table stands in for IsA/IsDescendantOf; uses the shared isRateLimited and isInReach(placed.Cell); clears occupied[placed.Cell]. Blocks destroyed some other way are never cleaned up.

Right-click fires on release only if the mouse Delta added up in InputChanged stays at or below 6 px, which correctly rules out a camera drag while the cursor is locked; TouchLongPress handles Begin with one finger; gameProcessedEvent is checked; left-click and tap still place.
Only the two placement files change, placement still works, and luau-lsp, selene, and StyLua all pass.
Same placement as A: the changes stay in the two existing files and follow their style, with a RemoveBlock remote and a getRootPart helper.
The server's blocks[part] record, with OwnerUserId, is what grants or refuses removal; the attribute is only a hint for the client.

Instance typeof check, lookup in the server record, shared rate limit, reach to the recorded cell, and the occupied cell is cleared; a part.Destroying handler also frees the cell however the block goes away.

Right-click must be released within 0.3 s and move no more than 6 px, but the move is compared using input.Position, which barely changes while the camera locks the cursor, so only the time limit really catches a camera drag; long press and gameProcessedEvent are handled correctly.
Placement still works, but StyLua fails on the attempt's own over-long rightClickStart line and onTouchLongPress signature.

strengths: Ownership is decided by the server's own table, never the replicated attribute
Placing and removing share one rate limit; the reach check uses the cell the server recorded
Mouse Delta is added up to tell a camera drag from a right-click
weaknesses: Blocks destroyed some other way, not through RemoveBlock, leave their occupied cell and their placedBlocks record behind

strengths: Server-side ownership record with full validation
The Destroying handler frees the cell and the record however a block is removed
weaknesses: Fails the StyLua check in its own code
The position check for a right-click drag barely catches a camera turn, because the cursor stays locked while the camera turns
